Narrative Tenses: Simple Past, Past Continuous, Past Perfect and Past Perfect Continuous
Narrative tenses are the grammatical structures you use to refer to the past time. You use them to tell stories and describe past events and states.
You use the Simple Past to talk about a finished action or state that happened at a definite time in the past.
We saw a wonderful film last night.
You use the Past Continuous to talk about an action in progress happening at a specific time in the past.
We were watching TV when someone knocked on the door.
You use the Past Perfect to talk about an action or state that happened before a past action or state.
When we arrived at the theater, the movie had already started.
You use the Past Perfect Continuous to talk about an action in progress that was happening before another past action.
When he arrived she had been waiting for over an hour!

Speculating About the Past with Different Degrees of Certainty
When you want to speculate (when you say what you think is true or not true about the past), you use different modal verbs to indicate the degree of certainty.
When you consider some present evidence and draw a reasonably certain conclusion about what happened in the past, you use must have and couldn't have plus the past participle of the verb.

Vanessa: So Peter, I know you believe in mercury retrograde and after the past couple weeks that I've had, I'm beginning to give credence to it too. I think all of the unusual things that have been happening lately must have been caused by the retrograde.
Peter: Yes, I definitely think the retrograde could have been responsible for any malfunction with electronics.
Vanessa: So do you also believe that your star sign dictates your personality and your relationships?
Peter: Yes, I do. I'm an Aquarius. We have been described as witty, clever, inventive and original.

Vanessa: Well, you are witty and you can be inventive. I remember when you were working at the first PR firm. You wrote a lot of really creative copy.
Peter: We can also be stubborn and rebellious. I remember when I had been working at that company for about 6 months and my supervisor started really critiquing my work. I had written a piece that I was really happy with and he edited it heavily. He tried to explain why he had made that edits that he did and I got really sarcastic with him. That's another trait of Aquarians.
Vanessa: I remember you telling me about that. If you hadn't spoken to him like that, you could have stayed there longer.

Peter: Yeah, that was the beginning of the end. It might have been better if I'd stayed there a bit longer, but I'm happy that I left. He was a Virgo ... not a good match for Aquarius!
Vanessa: Oh, then you must have been relieved when you could leave! What about now? Is your current manager a good match for you?
Peter: Yes, actually he is. He's a Gemini. Not many other signs get along well with Gemini but I tend to. You have to be pretty-laid back to deal with the Gemini personality.
Vanessa: Well, you are definitely laid-back!
